correct_completion: I would buy a new bike.
full_sentence: If I had more money, I would buy a new bike.
acceptable_variants: I would buy a new car.
I could buy a new bike.

options.text: I bought a new bike yesterday.
options.why_wrong: This is a past simple sentence about a real event, not a hypothetical result of the condition 'had more money'.

options.text: I would buy a new bike.
I will buy a new bike tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' is used for real future plans, but the second conditional needs 'would' to describe an unreal, imagined situation.

options.text: I buy a new bike every day.
options.why_wrong: This describes a habit in the present and does not complete the imagined condition set by 'if I had more money'.

grammar_focus: Second conditional with 'if' and 'would' for imagined situations
explanation: The stem uses 'if' with a past simple verb, so the result clause needs 'would' plus the base verb. Learners often mix up the tense of the result clause with the tense of the 'if' clause, so remember that both parts shift back together in the second conditional.
translation: Gdybym miał więcej pieniędzy, kupiłbym nowy rower.
